beats.trigger: ## Building Agent Systems
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: A system remembers, grows, and compounds. Chat doesn't.
beats.got: A slogan. 'Compounds' is the word every programme uses.

beats.trigger: (1) Bring a live challenge. (2) Verify your Confluence and OneDrive connectors.
beats.got: Homework with five items, and I haven't done any of it.

beats.trigger: **Evaluate** whether memory is compounding or growing
beats.got: The last bullet is the only one that sounds like a test I could run.

beats.trigger: What's the difference between asking an LLM a question and having an LLM maintain a knowledge base for you?
beats.got: Chat forgets and files don't. I already knew that.

beats.trigger: Connectors let the agent combine clues that live apart, like a wiki page and an email thread.
beats.got: It can read across Confluence and email, which is a bit more useful than a chat window.

beats.trigger: The guardrail: propose or draft only, do not send, edit, book, or change anything.
beats.got: It runs without being asked, and it is boxed in to drafting. That is more sober than I expected.

beats.trigger: Not a fit: *last year's re-org*, *becoming a better leader*, *understanding AI*.
beats.got: It tells me to pick something I actually own. At least it doesn't ask for a vision.

beats.trigger: Keep it narrow enough that 5–8 topic pages cover it.
beats.got: A small, bounded job. Fine.

beats.trigger: **Always comply with your company's AI policy.**
beats.got: Someone thought about the data policy. Our legal team will ask exactly this.

beats.trigger: If the agent starts reading before showing it, stop it, steer narrower, say *"continue"*.
beats.got: It sometimes runs off on its own, and you have to hold it back. Good that they say so.

beats.trigger: Push back, sharpen, add what's missing.
beats.got: I review a list the agent drafted.

beats.trigger: List (3), the NOT REACHABLE pile, stays a reference file unless you share it with the agent to save into `sources/`.
beats.got: Some of my material it cannot reach. Fair enough.

beats.trigger: Ask the agent to write a plan first and wait for your approval before it touches files.
beats.got: Approve first, then it acts. That is how I would run a project anyway.

beats.trigger: That list is your first quality check.
beats.got: It lists its own gaps. A tool that admits what it doesn't know is more than the last programmes did.

beats.trigger: Citations show whether the agent read the memory or the LLM filled in from training data.
beats.got: I can check whether it read my files or made it up. That is something I can test myself.

beats.trigger: Push back if a claim "got sharper" but the top didn't change. Chat cannot do this.
beats.got: New material revises the old pages instead of piling up. I could check that myself, and it is the first thing today that wasn't in the last three programmes.

beats.trigger: Reject the ones that miss; the agent applies the ones you approve.
beats.got: It proposes, I decide. The human stays in charge.

beats.trigger: If it is generic or leans on uncited knowledge, that shows where the memory is still thin.
beats.got: The test is whether the answer cites my files. If it doesn't, the memory is thin.

beats.trigger: so the system keeps getting better the more you feed it.
beats.got: 'Keeps getting better' is a claim. I'd need a few weeks of use before I believed it.

beats.trigger: The second batch made the first batch better. That is compounding.
beats.got: A name for what Phase 3 showed. Fine.

beats.trigger: An agent with no files is a chat.
beats.got: Files plus instructions make a system. I'd have said it more plainly.

beats.trigger: so old and new claims met and the ones that couldn't survive got cut.
beats.got: It reads the old pages as context when it writes the update. That explains why it sharpens.

beats.trigger: Keep the rules small and boring.
beats.got: Boring rules. I like that. Nobody sold me a revolution.

beats.trigger: No database, special tool or paid tier is needed.
beats.got: It is a folder of markdown files. No vendor lock-in, which my procurement people would like.

beats.trigger: Sharpen the memory, never the sources, or you lose the evidence.
beats.got: Keep the originals untouched so you can audit the summaries against them.

beats.trigger: *Generic AI becomes your AI when you build the memory it reads.*
beats.got: A brochure line.

beats.trigger: If a competitor could claim a page, the memory is growing but not compounding.
beats.got: A usable test: would a competitor write this page? If yes, it's generic.

beats.trigger: Most of what you know about your company sits in heads and corridors, and nobody has written it down.
beats.got: The agent only knows what we write down, and we don't write much down. True, and a bit uncomfortable.

beats.trigger: The agent writes the rules file from the session: what worked, what rubbed, what got repeated.
beats.got: The agent drafts the rules file from the session.

beats.trigger: What the agent leaves out is often the signal.
beats.got: Check what the summary omits. Same as reading a steering-group report.

beats.trigger: Watching where it bends is continuous improvement, done by hand.
beats.got: A miss becomes a rule. That is just old-fashioned quality management.

beats.trigger: The model will change under this. The memory will not.
beats.got: The folder is what lasts; the model gets swapped. That is a sensible way to look at the risk.

beats.trigger: Plain text: models read and write text best.
beats.got: Nothing new

beats.trigger: Module 3 splits work against that week of runs; without it the split is guesswork.
beats.got: I'm expected to run something for a week before the next session. My calendar says no.

beats.trigger: Pick the one you would read tomorrow morning.
beats.got: Pick a daily job I would actually read. Honest enough.

beats.trigger: sign in with your work account
beats.got: Calendar access means IT and a data-protection question. Someone will ask it.

beats.trigger: Give your daily output the look and feel of your company's website (colours, typography, headers, voice).
beats.got: Making the output look like our website. Cosmetic.

beats.trigger: Have the agent interview you on the job, output shape and hard boundary, then write its instruction file.
beats.got: Another interview, another file. Same move again.

beats.trigger: Save, then click **Run now** once.
beats.got: I schedule it, run it once, and see the output. I'd actually do that.

beats.trigger: Comical or wrong days: what was missing from the memory?
beats.got: They expect it to produce wrong days and call that useful. A candid thing to say.

beats.trigger: after a week the memory has more edge.
beats.got: A bold claim about a week I haven't had yet.

beats.trigger: [Agent Trigger List, After Module 2]
beats.got: More reading. I'll skip it.

beats.trigger: **Time:** 40 minutes total. 25 reading, 5 noting takeaways, 10 on the helper-agent primer.
beats.got: Forty minutes of prework. That is exactly the point where I stop.

beats.trigger: Keep the first version proposal-only: the agent drafts, ranks, or prepares; you decide what leaves the system.
beats.got: Start with agents that only draft, and decide yourself what gets sent.

take_homes: Phase 3 was the only thing that was new. When you add a source, the pages get tighter instead of just longer. I could check that myself.
The agent's answers have to cite my files, otherwise it is making things up. That is a test I can run on any answer.
Keep the agent proposal-only and keep the knowledge in a plain folder, not in a vendor's tool.

monday.move: Nothing on Monday. If a quiet hour turns up this week, I might build a memory on one real open item and check whether the citations hold.
monday.stop_condition: The answers don't cite my files, or it takes more than an hour.
monday.blocker: A calendar full of steering groups, plus no clarity on what our data policy allows.

misconception.why: New sources reworked the old pages and I could check the result. Memory in files is something I haven't seen in agile, SAFe or OKRs. I still think the 'compounding' language is overselling it, and I'm not yet convinced it holds beyond a toy case.

one_line: Mostly the usual wrapper, but the memory exercise has a test you can run yourself, and that's more than the last three programmes offered.
